To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prefetching reduces the expected response time of a document if the document's lifetime is shorter than its average access time and the client has a sufficient amount of idle time.

(1) Prefetching reduces the response-time of a document only if the document's lifetime is sufficiently short; (2) The optimal number of documents to prefetched in a given think period is determined by the document's average lifetime, the think period, and the number of documents in the cache; (3) Prefetching is most effective when the cache is small and the average document lifetime is short; and (4) Prefetching should be combined with passive caching to maximize performance
prefetching is effective only if the number of documents to be prefetched is carefully chosen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of a novel client-side caching system that integrates passive caching and document prefetching.
the performance analysis of a client side caching/prefetch system.

a fundamental question: When is prefetching beneficial for a Web caching system? Our results provide an answer to this question and show that prefetching can be a very effective tool for reducing the average response time.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prefetching reduces the mean response time of a document if the document lifetime is less than a certain threshold, which is determined by the system parameters.
prefetching can be beneficial for Web caching, and that the optimal prefetching strategy depends on the system parameters.
prefetching reduces the mean response time of a Web document only if it is used judiciously.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, under certain conditions, prefetching is an effective means of reducing the average latency for Web document requests.

, for the Web caching system we consider, prefetching reduces the expected response time of a document if the number of documents that can be cached at the client is at least 2.2 times larger than the number that can be cached in the proxy.
prefetching can be a very effective tool for Web caching, but its performance is highly sensitive to the system's parameters and to the nature of the traffic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under certain conditions, prefetching can significantly reduce the response time of Web documents.
prefetching can reduce the average response time, even if some of the prefetched documents are never accessed by the user.
, for a given system configuration, there exists an optimal number of documents to be prefetched during the client's think time.
